verdict.rationale: Crossplane says it exposes declarative APIs that "humans, automation, and AI systems can safely act on" and applies Kubernetes RBAC to everything it manages. A community comment adds that callers get permission only at the abstraction interface they use, which supports least-privilege scoping for an agent. Nothing in the evidence shows a plan/preview step for infrastructure changes or an approval gate that blocks unapproved applies; CLI rendering covers only composition functions, and Composition Revisions are versioning, not review. Missing for 10: documented plan/diff preview of infrastructure changes, human review/approval gates before apply, agent-specific credential-scoping guidance, independent hands-on corroboration.
